answer: An agent marketplace requires a $100 bond per active seller, whether it trades violet dye, models a volcanic plume, or plans a summit. Each bond supports only one open contract and stays locked for 30 days after completion. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000 in capital. Splitting identities cannot increase trading capacity per dollar, so an attacker must fund every extra slot and bear the cost of keeping that money idle.
